correctness.rationale: For each fixed b>=3, every maximum-run start has form b²c by the inspected Gohn et al. boundary classification. The neighboring offsets force product of nonzero digits of c to equal 1, and divisibility at offsets 1,...,b-1 imposes exactly M_b|c. The remaining offsets are guaranteed by definition of the first nondivisor of b. Prime-power splitting M_b=M0*M1 gives precisely r forced trailing zeros and a coprime modulus. Fourier inversion on M1 and uniform nontrivial character bounds prove effective shell equidistribution and all boundary cases M1=1 and zero shells. Fixed leading-digit cylinders give weak Cantor convergence; two nested cutoffs expose genuinely distinct constants for cumulative growth. The stdlib finite checker independently compares digit enumeration, actual membership, and exhaustive detected runs for 10 small bases, 80 shells; finite tests do not prove infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The full inspected JIS 2022 paper obtains extremal run length and a boundary classification, but not the exact set of all starts, any quantitative count by digit length, the limiting Cantor law, or nonexistence of a global scaling constant. Restricted-digit residue equidistribution is an existing method (Banks--Shparlinski, 2004) and not claimed as new. A later Zuckerman-counting paper addresses a different product convention. No covering result was found among actual targeted mathematical queries. Residual priority uncertainty, especially general digit restrictions, explicitly retained.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished result may already enumerate maximal b-prodigious run starts.

value.rationale: For an explicit extremal phenomenon whose attainable maximal length was singled out by prior research, the theorem determines the entire starting set and its infinite sharp digit-shell census, with all noncoprime factors handled. Its nontrivial Cantor positional law and two distinct cumulative normalization limits are meaningful structural density data; not merely restatement of a generic modular counting lemma, nor a finite numerical table.
